points: This carryover audit supplements only G2 and G3; G0/G4/G5/G1 are inherited from the existing candidate record and were not re-adjudicated.

A real Chrome session read the complete first two US-English Google result pages. Page one mixed one exact Google Cloud implementation with adjacent Google Cloud concept pages and AWS multi-party-approval material; page two fell into AWS, Azure, and generic backup content, establishing a quality cliff without video, wiki, major-media, or strong-brand-homepage takeover.
G2=pass: the two-page SERP is mixed inner-document and generic material rather than a durable strong-brand or media takeover.

The exact Google Cloud page is a complete tutorial for protecting Backup and DR project liens with Privileged Access Manager, including role audit, a custom lien permission, entitlement configuration, request, approval, execution, and cleanup.

G3=pass: only that Google Cloud tutorial completes the exact GCP project-lien plus PAM task. Google Cloud concept pages cross-link or summarize the mechanism, while the AWS analogue uses a different cloud resource and approval system and is not a second exact implementation.
This is not veto_window_bet: fewer than two exact implementations are visibly indexed, rather than several obvious implementations being temporarily hidden.

Window estimate is weeks, expiring 2026-09-20. The dated automatic-lien rollout creates near-term demand, but the official exact guide already ranks first and cross-cloud semantic collision limits the gap.

Invalidation conditions: two or more free and stable GCP project-lien plus PAM completion pages enter the SERP; the PAM entitlement or resourcemanager.projects.updateLiens setup path changes; the Backup and DR automatic project-lien behavior is withdrawn or rescheduled.
Caveat: Chrome used a signed-in Google session with gl=us, hl=en, pws=0; the result footer reported that results were not personalized, while safe=active and ssui=on were appended by Google.
